newsitem.title: USA: Internet pizza shop opens virtual order line.
newsitem.headline: Internet pizza shop opens virtual order line.

text.p: In a case of life imitating art, a Seattle-based startup company is making it possible for computer users to order pizza over the Internet.

Entrepreneur Tim Glass said Monday he was inspired by the 1995 movie "The Net" to develop CyberSlice Inc., which opened its virtual doors Sunday and allows Internet hounds to order from hundreds of pizzerias in four cities.

Glass said while U.S. consumers -- who order some 500 million pizzas annually -- might find the telephone more convenient now, ultimately the computer network will be as easy as using a television remote control.
"Think about ordering food over the telephone -- you can't see the menu or compare prices," Glass said. "Someday we're going to laugh about it."

While several local and national pizza restaurants including Pizza Hut allow users to order by electronic mail, Glass said CyberSlice is the first service that gives users a list of pizzerias that are open and deliver to their address.

The site on the Internet's World Wide Web (http://www.cyberslice.com) provides menus and prices and allows consumers to place orders that are converted into automated voice messages that call the restaurants' order phones.
"The merchant doesn't have to buy a computer, a fax machine or even change their procedures," said Glass, who founded the company along with a partner from a previous software venture.
Restaurants pay nothing to be listed but pay CyberSlice from 50 cents to $3 for every order placed, depending on the size of the order.
While Cyberslice will list all restaurants identically, the company ultimately plans to allow restaurants to buy promotional space and offer coupons, much as they would in a telephone directory.
The company also is pursuing possible corporate sponsorships of the Web site.
Glass said that within three weeks the service would include listings for 1,000 pizzerias in the Seattle, Boston, New York and San Francisco areas.
Glass said he hopes to expand rapidly to cover a substantial number of U.S. cities by mid-1997 and ultimately wants to apply the concept to other food and non-food businesses.
"Chinese food would be a natural," he said.
Among Cyberslice's initial investors is Ford Smith, founder of the Petsmart Inc. chain, Glass said.
